reply.english: I don't know, but it's cloudy.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير إيلي، شو الطقس اليوم؟
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH elkheer Eeli, shu eTTa2s elyoom?
dialogue.english: Good morning Elie, what's the weather like today?

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور. الجو مغيّم شوي بس مش برد
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH ennoor. eljaw mghayyem shwayy bas mish bard
dialogue.english: Good morning. It's a bit cloudy but not cold.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: في رطوبة كتير اليوم كمان
dialogue.transliteration: fi ruTuube ktiir elyoom kamaan
dialogue.english: It's very humid today too.

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: إي، هيك بتكون ببيروت. رح تشتّي بكرا برأيك؟
dialogue.transliteration: ee, heik betkuun bi Bayroot. ra7 teshti bukra bra2yak?
dialogue.english: Yes, that's how it is in Beirut. Do you think it'll rain tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: ما بعرف. شو بيقولوا بالنشرة؟
dialogue.transliteration: ma ba3ref. shu biquulu bennashre?
dialogue.english: I don't know. What do they say in the forecast?

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: بيقولوا رح يكون في هوا كتير وشتي بالليل
dialogue.transliteration: biquulu ra7 ykuun fi hawa ktiir w shiti billeel
dialogue.english: They say there'll be a lot of wind and rain at night.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: خلص، لازم آخد شمسية معي
dialogue.transliteration: khalaS, laazem aakhod shamseeye ma3i
dialogue.english: OK, I need to take an umbrella with me.

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: إي أكيد، وخودي جاكيت كمان، الدنيا برد برّا
dialogue.transliteration: ee akiid, w khodi jaakeet kamaan, eddinye bard barra
dialogue.english: Yes of course, and take a jacket too, it's cold outside.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: يسلمو عالنصيحة
dialogue.transliteration: yislamu 3alnaSii7a
dialogue.english: Thanks for the advice.

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: ولو، ما في شي. إن شاء الله بيصير الجو حلو
dialogue.transliteration: wallaw, ma fi shi. in shaa2 allah biSiir eljaw 7ilu
dialogue.english: Not at all, it's nothing. God willing the weather will turn nice.

dialogue.speaker: Nadine
dialogue.arabic: إن شاء الله. مع السلامة!
dialogue.transliteration: in shaa2 allah. ma3 essalaame!
dialogue.english: God willing. Bye!

dialogue.speaker: Elie
dialogue.arabic: الله معك، بشوفك
dialogue.transliteration: allah ma3ik, bshuufik
dialogue.english: God be with you, see you.

response.english: Yes, take an umbrella with you.

pair.arabic: في هوا كتير اليوم، مش هيك؟
pair.transliteration: fi hawa ktiir elyoom, mish heik?
pair.english: There's a lot of wind today, isn't there?
Is it going to rain tomorrow?

lessons.culture: In Lebanon people open a conversation with the weather all the time, and "الدنيا" is often used for it: "الدنيا برد", "الدنيا حر". Along the coast the summer is humid, so "في رطوبة" comes up almost every day.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "شو الطقس اليوم؟" Say it is nice and sunny.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but sounds like a formal weather report, not everyday speech.

exercises.tip: Everyday speech says "حلو", not "صحو".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "عم بتشتّي هلّق؟" but you can see the sun. Say no, the sun is out.

too_formal.feedback: Grammatically fine, but far more elaborate and bookish than a quick spoken answer.

exercises.tip: A short, quick answer is the natural one.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عم _____ برّا من الصبح." (It has been raining outside since morning.)

too_formal.feedback: This is Modern Standard Arabic; the everyday verb for rain is "شتّى", used as "عم بتشتّي".

exercises.tip: "عم بتشتّي" is the ordinary way to say it is raining right now.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "لازم تاخد _____ معك، رح تشتّي." (umbrella)

too_formal.feedback: This is the standard Arabic word for umbrella; everyday Lebanese says "شمسية".

exercises.tip: "شمسية" is the everyday word for umbrella.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "It's cold today."

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but "بارد" as a plain adjective sounds written; "الدنيا برد" is how it is said.

exercises.tip: "الدنيا" stands in for the weather: "الدنيا برد", "الدنيا حر".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "There's a lot of wind today."

too_formal.feedback: This is formal weather-report language; people say "هوا", not "رياح".

exercises.tip: "هوا" means wind as well as air.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "It's cloudy"?

too_formal.feedback: This is a literary description of clouds, not the everyday remark.

exercises.tip: "مغيّم" is the simple word for cloudy.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "It's humid today"?

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but reads like a report; in speech people say "في رطوبة".

exercises.tip: "في" means "there is", so "في رطوبة" is literally "there is humidity".

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "شمسية / لازم / معك / تاخد"

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but formal; "لازم" plus a verb without "أن" is the spoken pattern.

exercises.tip: "لازم" is followed straight by the verb: "لازم تاخد".

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "برّا / هلّق / عم / بتشتّي"

too_formal.feedback: Correct Arabic, but written-style; "برّا" and "هلّق" are the spoken words.

exercises.tip: "عم" plus "بـ" verb means it is happening right now.

phrases.english: In winter it gets very cold in Beirut.

phrases.arabic: مَا بِحِبّ الشِّتِي لِأَنّو بِيبِرّد كْتِير
phrases.transliteration: ma bi7ebb eshshiti la2anno biberrad ktiir

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: شو رأيك، أي فصل بتحب أكتر؟
dialogue.transliteration: shu ra2yak, ayy faSl bti7eb aktar?
dialogue.english: What do you think, which season do you like most?

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: بحب الصيف أكتر شي، بنزل عالبحر
dialogue.transliteration: bi7ebb eSSeef aktar shi, bnezzel 3alba7er
dialogue.english: I like summer best, I go down to the sea.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: أنا لأ، الصيف بلبنان طويل والدنيا رطوبة
dialogue.transliteration: ana la2, eSSeef bi lebnaan Tawiil w eddinye ruTuube
dialogue.english: Not me, summer in Lebanon is long and it's humid.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: وإنتِ أي فصل بتحبّي؟
dialogue.transliteration: w enti ayy faSl bti7ebbi?
dialogue.english: And which season do you like?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: الربيع أحلى فصل عندي، بحب ريحة الشتي
dialogue.transliteration: erribee3 a7la faSl 3indi, bi7ebb ree7et eshshiti
dialogue.english: Spring is my favourite, I like the smell of rain.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: والشتي؟ ما بتحبّيه؟
dialogue.transliteration: w eshshiti? ma bti7ebbo?
dialogue.english: And winter? You don't like it?

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: لأ، بيبرد كتير وبتشتّي طول الوقت
dialogue.transliteration: la2, biberrad ktiir w bteshti Tool elwa2et
dialogue.english: No, it gets very cold and it rains all the time.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: بس عالجبل بيحلا، عم بتتلّج هلّق
dialogue.transliteration: bas 3aljabal bi7la, 3am betetallaj halla2
dialogue.english: But on the mountain it gets nice, it's snowing now.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: صح، بالشتي لازم تلبس شي تقيل
dialogue.transliteration: Sa7, bishshiti laazem telbas shi te2eel
dialogue.english: True, in winter you need to wear something heavy.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: بالضبط. الطقس بيتغيّر كتير بين الفصول بلبنان
dialogue.transliteration: biDDabT. eTTa2s bitghayyar ktiir been elfuSuul bi lebnaan
dialogue.english: Exactly. The weather changes a lot between the seasons in Lebanon.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.arabic: إي، وبالبقاع الصيف حامي وناشف
dialogue.transliteration: ee, w bilbi2aa3 eSSeef 7aami w naashef
dialogue.english: Yes, and in the Bekaa summer is hot and dry.

dialogue.speaker: Rami
dialogue.arabic: خلص، بالشتي منطلع عالجبل سوا
dialogue.transliteration: khalaS, bishshiti mneTla3 3aljabal sawa
dialogue.english: Fine, in winter we'll go up the mountain together.

pair.english: Which season do you like most?
What season are we in now?
Is it snowing on the mountain?

lessons.culture: In Lebanon you can swim in the sea and ski on the same day in spring, so people are proud of their seasons. The coast is hot and humid in summer, the Bekaa is hot and dry, and the mountains get snow from around December to March.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "أي فصل بتحب أكتر؟" Say you like summer best.

too_formal.item: أفضّل فصل الصيف على سائر الفصول
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; the spoken way is "بحب ... أكتر شي".

exercises.tip: "أكتر شي" means "the most of anything".

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "بأي فصل نحنا هلّق؟" Say we are in fall.

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but stiff; in speech "نحنا" replaces "نحن" and the sentence is short.

exercises.tip: Lebanese says "نحنا" for "we".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عم بتتلّج _____." (It's snowing on the mountain.)

too_formal.feedback: This is formal MSA; the spoken verb is "تلّج" and "على" shrinks to "عـ".

exercises.tip: "على" often shortens to "عـ" and joins the next word.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بالخريف بيوقع _____ عن الشجر." (leaves)

too_formal.feedback: This is the written plural; "الورق" is the everyday word for leaves on a tree.

exercises.tip: "ورق" means both paper and leaves.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I don't like winter because it gets very cold."
exercises.answer: مَا بِحِبّ الشِّتِي لِأَنّو بِيبِرّد كْتِير
accepted: مَا بِحِبّ الشِّتِي لِأَنّو بِيبِرّد كْتِير
ما بحب الشتا لأنو بيبرد كتير
ما بحب الشتي لأنو الدنيا بتبرد كتير
ما بحب الشتي لأنو برد كتير
ma bi7ebb eshshiti la2anno biberrad ktiir

too_formal.item: لا أحب الشتاء لأن الطقس شديد البرودة
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "ما بحب" and "لأنو" are the everyday forms.

exercises.tip: "ما" plus "بحب" is the spoken way to say "I don't like".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Summer in Lebanon is long."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct but formal; "بلبنان" joins "في" to the noun in speech.

exercises.tip: "بـ" before a place name means "in".

exercises.prompt: Which word means "spring"?

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal way to name the season; in speech just "الربيع".

exercises.tip: "الربيع" spring, "الصيف" summer, "الخريف" fall, "الشتي" winter.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "The weather changes a lot between the seasons"?

too_formal.item: تتبدّل أحوال الطقس كثيراً بين الفصول
too_formal.feedback: This is a written phrasing; "بيتغيّر" and "كتير" are the spoken forms.

exercises.tip: "بـ" plus a verb is the present: "بيتغيّر" changes.

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "تقيل / لازم / بالشتي / شي / تلبس"

too_formal.item: في الشتاء يجب أن ترتدي ملابس ثقيلة
too_formal.feedback: Correct but written; "شي تقيل" is the spoken "something heavy".

exercises.tip: "شي" means "something" and "ق" is said as a glottal stop in "تقيل".

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "الربيع / أحلى / فصل / عندي"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "أحلى فصل عندي" is how people say it.

exercises.tip: "عندي" here means "in my view".

phrases.arabic: بِدّك بُوط بِالشِّتِي لِأَنّو بِتْشْتِّي كْتِير
phrases.transliteration: biddak boot bishshiti la2anno bteshti ktiir

phrases.arabic: إِلْبِس شِي مِرِيح لِأَنّو رَح نِمْشِي كْتِير
phrases.transliteration: elbas shi mreei7 la2anno ra7 nemshi ktiir

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: هادي، شو ألبس اليوم؟ الدنيا مغيّمة
dialogue.transliteration: Haadi, shu elbas elyoom? eddinye mghayyme
dialogue.english: Hadi, what should I wear today? It's cloudy.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: إلبسي جاكيت، الدنيا برد برّا
dialogue.transliteration: elbasi jaakeet, eddinye bard barra
dialogue.english: Wear a jacket, it's cold outside.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: وبولوفر تحتو؟
dialogue.transliteration: w boolover ta7to?
dialogue.english: And a sweater under it?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: إي، وخودي شمسية كمان، رح تشتّي بعد الظهر
dialogue.transliteration: ee, w khodi shamseeye kamaan, ra7 teshti ba3d eDDuhur
dialogue.english: Yes, and take an umbrella too, it's going to rain in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: ما عندي شمسية، نسيتها عالشغل
dialogue.transliteration: ma 3indi shamseeye, nsiitha 3ashshoghol
dialogue.english: I don't have an umbrella, I forgot it at work.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: خدي شمسيتي، أنا عندي معطف بالسيارة
dialogue.transliteration: khdi shamseeyti, ana 3indi mi3Taf bissayyaara
dialogue.english: Take my umbrella, I have a coat in the car.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: يسلمو! لازم إلبس بوط كمان؟
dialogue.transliteration: yislamu! laazem elbas boot kamaan?
dialogue.english: Thanks! Do I need to wear boots too?

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: لأ، هيك منيح. بس إلبسي شي مريح، رح نمشي كتير
dialogue.transliteration: la2, heik mnii7. bas elbasi shi mreei7, ra7 nemshi ktiir
dialogue.english: No, this is fine. But wear something comfortable, we're going to walk a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: تمام. ما بدّي إبرد متل المرة الفاتت
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. ma biddi ebrad mitl elmarra elfaayte
dialogue.english: OK. I don't want to get cold like last time.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: إي، وقتها ما لبستي جاكيت وبردتي
dialogue.transliteration: ee, wa2ta ma lbesti jaakeet w bridti
dialogue.english: Yes, that time you didn't wear a jacket and you got cold.

dialogue.speaker: Layal
dialogue.arabic: صح! يلا، نص ساعة وبكون جاهزة
dialogue.transliteration: Sa7! yalla, niSS saa3a w bekuun jaahze
dialogue.english: True! Come on, half an hour and I'll be ready.

dialogue.speaker: Hadi
dialogue.arabic: تمام، بستناكي تحت
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, bestannaki ta7et
dialogue.english: OK, I'll wait for you downstairs.

response.english: Because I didn't wear a jacket.

pair.english: What's your favourite colour in sweaters?
What do you wear in fall?

lessons.culture: In Lebanon the coast is mild while the mountains a short drive away are much colder, so people leave in the morning with a jacket and take it off later. Advice like "خود شمسية" or "إلبس جاكيت" is said freely between friends and family, and is taken as care, not as bossiness.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "شو ألبس اليوم؟" It is cold. Tell them to wear a jacket.

too_formal.item: يجب أن ترتدي سترة لأن الطقس بارد
too_formal.feedback: This is correct but formal; a friend just says "إلبس" and the reason.

exercises.tip: "إلبس" is the command "wear"; "إلبسي" is for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "ليش بردت؟" Say you did not wear a jacket.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "ما" before the verb is the spoken negative, not "لم".

exercises.tip: "ما" plus a past verb says "did not".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "حط _____ الشمس، الشمس قوية." (sunglasses)

too_formal.feedback: This is the written spelling and pronunciation; everyday Lebanese says "نضارة".

exercises.tip: "حط" means "put on", and "نضارة الشمس" is sun glasses.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "بالشتي بدك _____ لأنو بتشتّي كتير." (boots)

too_formal.feedback: This is a formal description of the shoe; everyday Lebanese says "بوط".

exercises.tip: "بدك" means "you need" or "you want".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Wear a sweater, it's cold."

too_formal.feedback: This is correct formal Arabic; "كنزة" is understood but "بولوفر" is what is said.

exercises.tip: "بولوفر" is the everyday word for sweater.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I forgot the raincoat at home."

too_formal.item: نسيت المعطف الواقي من المطر في المنزل
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "البيت" is home in speech, not "المنزل".

exercises.tip: "بالبيت" or "عالبيت" both say "at home".

exercises.prompt: Which one means "sunglasses"?

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal written name; in speech "نضارة الشمس".

exercises.tip: "شمسية" is umbrella, "نضارة" is glasses; do not mix them.

exercises.prompt: What protects you from the sun?

too_formal.feedback: This is the standard Arabic word for hat; in Lebanese speech a sun hat is "برنيطة".

exercises.tip: "البرنيطة" is a hat; "البوط" are boots.

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "شورت / بلبس / بالصيف / وتيشيرت"

too_formal.item: في الصيف أرتدي سروالاً قصيراً وقميصاً
too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "بلبس" is I wear in speech.

exercises.tip: "بـ" plus a verb, "بلبس", is "I wear".

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "لأنو / مريح / إلبس / شي / رح / نمشي / كتير"
exercises.answer: إِلْبِس شِي مِرِيح لِأَنّو رَح نِمْشِي كْتِير
accepted: إِلْبِس شِي مِرِيح لِأَنّو رَح نِمْشِي كْتِير
البس شي مريح لأنو رح نمشي كتير
لأنو رح نمشي كتير إلبس شي مريح

too_formal.item: ارتدِ شيئاً مريحاً لأننا سنمشي كثيراً
too_formal.feedback: Correct but written; "رح" builds the future and "شي" means "something".

exercises.tip: "رح" before a verb means "will".

phrases.arabic: الجَو مِش مِنِيح، لَازِم نِلْغِي الطَّلْعَة
phrases.transliteration: eljaw mish mnii7, laazem nelghi eTTal3a

phrases.arabic: مَا فِينِي إِطْلِع، الجَو حَامِي كْتِير
بِمَا إِنّو رَح تِشْتِّي، خَلِينَا نِأَجّل السَّهْرَة
phrases.transliteration: bima 2anno ra7 teshti, khallina ne2ajjel essahre

phrases.arabic: طُول مَا الجَو مِنِيح، مِنْضِلّ نِطْلِع

reply.english: No, I haven't seen it yet.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: مرحبا ريما، شفتي نشرة الطقس؟
dialogue.transliteration: mar7aba Reema, shufti nashret eTTa2s?
dialogue.english: Hello Rima, did you see the weather forecast?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: أهلين كريم، إي شفتا. بكرا رح تشتّي
dialogue.transliteration: ahlayn Kareem, ee shifta. bukra ra7 teshti
dialogue.english: Hi Karim, yes I saw it. It's going to rain tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: يعني منأجّل رحلة الجبل؟
dialogue.transliteration: ya3ni mne2ajjel re7let eljabal?
dialogue.english: So we'll postpone the mountain trip?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: إي، إذا شتّت بكرا منأجّلها
dialogue.transliteration: ee, iza shattet bukra mne2ajjilha
dialogue.english: Yes, if it rains tomorrow we'll postpone it.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: طيب، شو رأيك نقعد بالبيت بكرا؟
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, shu ra2yak ne2od bilbeet bukra?
dialogue.english: OK, what do you think about staying home tomorrow?

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: أنا بفضّل نطلع نتمشّى إذا الجو حلو
dialogue.transliteration: ana bfaDDel neTla3 netmasha iza eljaw 7ilu
dialogue.english: I prefer to go out for a walk if the weather is nice.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: إي، طول ما الجو منيح منضل نطلع
dialogue.transliteration: ee, Tool ma eljaw mnii7 mnDall neTla3
dialogue.english: Yes, as long as the weather is good we'll keep going out.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: واليوم؟ الجو حلو، يلا نروح عالحديقة
dialogue.transliteration: w elyoom? eljaw 7ilu, yalla nruu7 3al7adii2a
dialogue.english: And today? The weather is nice, let's go to the park.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: اليوم الدنيا حر كتير، ما فيني إطلع
dialogue.transliteration: elyoom eddinye 7arr ktiir, ma fiini iTla3
dialogue.english: Today it's very hot, I can't go out.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: طيب، الليلة منقعد عالبلكون؟ الجو بيكون لطيف
dialogue.transliteration: Tayyeb, elleele mne2od 3albalkoon? eljaw bikuun laTiif
dialogue.english: Fine, shall we sit on the balcony tonight? The weather will be pleasant.

dialogue.speaker: Karim
dialogue.arabic: فكرة منيحة، تمام
dialogue.transliteration: fikra mnii7a, tamaam
dialogue.english: Good idea, OK.

dialogue.speaker: Rima
dialogue.arabic: تمام، منحكي بالليل إن شاء الله
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam, mne7ki billeel in shaa2 allah
dialogue.english: OK, we'll talk in the evening, God willing.

pair.english: Did you see the weather forecast?

response.english: Yes, it's going to rain tomorrow.

pair.english: What do you think about staying home today?
Shall we go to the park today?

response.english: If the weather is nice, yes.

pair.english: If it rains tomorrow, what do we do?

lessons.culture: In Lebanon weekend outings to the mountain, the sea or the Bekaa depend a lot on the weather, and plans are usually left open with "إن شاء الله". When the weather turns, people postpone with "منأجّل" rather than cancel for good.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks: "شو رأيك نقعد بالبيت اليوم؟" It is pouring. Agree.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiff; "فكرة منيحة" is the natural short answer.

exercises.tip: "منيح" is the everyday word for good.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks: "بدنا نطلع نتمشّى؟" It is far too hot. Say you can't go out.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "ما فيني" is how "I can't" is said.

exercises.tip: "فيني" means "I am able to".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إذا الطقس حلو، منروح _____." (to the park)

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal preposition; in speech "على" shrinks to "عـ" after "روح".

exercises.tip: "منروح" is "we go", with "من" marking "we".

exercises.prompt: Complete: "إذا شتّت بكرا، _____ الرحلة." (we'll postpone the trip)

too_formal.feedback: This is the formal future; in speech "من" plus the verb means "we".

exercises.tip: "منأجّل" is "we postpone", and it also works as "we will".

exercises.prompt: Translate: "Did you see the weather forecast?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; nobody says "هل" to start a question in speech.

exercises.tip: "شفت" is "did you see", and "شفتي" is for a woman.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "The trip to the mountain depends on the weather."

too_formal.item: تعتمد الرحلة إلى الجبل على حالة الطقس
too_formal.feedback: This is correct but written; "عالطقس" is how it sounds in speech.

exercises.tip: "بتتوقّف عـ" means "depends on".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "Let's postpone the evening gathering"?

too_formal.feedback: This is formal; "خلينا" is the everyday "let us".

exercises.tip: "خلينا" plus a verb means "let's".

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means "As long as the weather's good, we'll keep going out"?
exercises.answer: طُول مَا الجَو مِنِيح، مِنْضِلّ نِطْلِع
accepted: طُول مَا الجَو مِنِيح، مِنْضِلّ نِطْلِع
طول ما الطقس منيح، منضل نطلع
طول ما الجو حلو، منضل نطلع
Tool ma eljaw mnii7 mnDall neTla3
Tool ma eljaw mnii7, mnDall neTla3
options: طُول مَا الجَو مِنِيح، مِنْضِلّ نِطْلِع

too_formal.item: ما دام الطقس جيداً سنستمر بالخروج
too_formal.feedback: This is correct but formal; "طول ما" is the everyday "as long as".

exercises.tip: "منضل" plus a verb means "we keep doing it".

exercises.prompt: Put in order: "الجو / حلو / يلا / نطلع / نتمشّى"

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; "يلا" is the everyday "come on".

exercises.tip: "يلا" invites everyone to start.

exercises.prompt: Put the pieces in order: "خلينا نأجّل السهرة / بما إنو / رح تشتّي"
exercises.answer: بما إنو رح تشتّي خلينا نأجّل السهرة
accepted: بما إنو رح تشتّي خلينا نأجّل السهرة
بِمَا إِنّو رَح تِشْتِّي، خَلِينَا نِأَجّل السَّهْرَة
خلينا نأجّل السهرة بما إنو رح تشتّي
bima 2anno ra7 teshti khallina ne2ajjel essahre

too_formal.feedback: Correct but written; "بما إنو" and "رح" are spoken.

exercises.tip: "بما إنو" means "since" and starts the reason.

challenge.title: Plan Your Day Around the Weather
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Lebanese conversation, at least 10 lines, between two friends deciding what to do today based on the weather. It must include asking about the weather, describing it with at least two weather words, a mention of the season, advice on what to wear, and a decision to go out or stay home.
required_elements: A question asking what the weather is like, using شو الطقس.
At least two different weather descriptions, such as الدنيا حر, الدنيا برد, الجو مغيّم or عم بتشتّي.
A mention of a season, using a word like الصيف, الشتي, الربيع or الخريف.
Advice on what to wear, using لازم تلبس or إلبس.
A reminder to take an umbrella, using خود شمسية or لازم تاخد شمسية.
A condition using إذا الطقس حلو or إذا شتّت.
A final decision to go out (منطلع) or stay home (منقعد بالبيت).

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير بلال، شو الطقس اليوم؟
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH elkheer Bilaal, shu eTTa2s elyoom?
dialogue.english: Good morning Bilal, what's the weather like today?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: صباح النور. الجو مغيّم شوي بس مش برد كتير
dialogue.transliteration: SabaaH ennoor. eljaw mghayyem shwayy bas mish bard ktiir
dialogue.english: Good morning. It's a bit cloudy but not too cold.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: بأي فصل نحنا هلّق؟ الورق عم بيوقع
dialogue.transliteration: bi2ayy faSl ne7na halla2? elwara2 3am biwa2a3
dialogue.english: What season are we in now? The leaves are falling.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: نحنا بالخريف، وبيبرد شوي بالليل
dialogue.transliteration: ne7na bilkhareef, w biberrad shwayy billeel
dialogue.english: We're in fall, and it gets a bit cold at night.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: شفت نشرة الطقس؟ في احتمال شتي بعد الظهر
dialogue.transliteration: shift nashret eTTa2s? fi i7timaal shiti ba3d eDDuhur
dialogue.english: Did you see the forecast? There is a chance of rain in the afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: لأ ما شفتا، بس خود شمسية معك على كل حال
dialogue.transliteration: la2 ma shifta, bas khod shamseeye ma3ak 3ala kell 7aal
dialogue.english: No I didn't, but take an umbrella with you anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: إي، وإنتَ إلبس جاكيت خفيف، الدنيا رح تبرد
dialogue.transliteration: ee, w enta elbas jaakeet khafiif, eddinye ra7 tibrad
dialogue.english: Yes, and you wear a light jacket, it's going to get cold.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: تمام. إذا الطقس حلو بعد الظهر، منروح عالحديقة
dialogue.transliteration: tamaam. iza eTTa2s 7ilu ba3d eDDuhur, mnruu7 3al7adii2a
dialogue.english: OK. If the weather is nice in the afternoon, we'll go to the park.

dialogue.speaker: Yara
dialogue.arabic: وإذا شتّت، منقعد بالبيت ومنشرب شاي
dialogue.transliteration: w iza shattet, mne2od bilbeet w mneshrab shaay
dialogue.english: And if it rains, we'll stay home and drink tea.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: فكرة منيحة، منحكي الساعة تلاتة
dialogue.transliteration: fikra mnii7a, mne7ki essaa3a tlaate
dialogue.english: Good idea, we'll talk at three.
